decisionMemo.businessProblem: A manufacturer with a healthy 26% blended gross margin is considering an expanded, deeper-discounted volume agreement with its #1 customer that would push top-3 concentration above 50%. Competing hypotheses: (1) the blended margin proves the customer mix is healthy and growing with the best customers is sound; (2) the blended margin masks that the heavily discounted, high-cost-to-serve top-3 accounts may be substantially less profitable - or even unprofitable on a fully-loaded basis - than the smaller accounts that subsidize the blend, so deepening discounts and concentration could erode profit and increase fragility; (3) a mix. The discounting and the higher cost-to-serve of the big accounts are visible, but per-customer profitability has never been computed because the company allocates overhead plant-wide.
